findings.title: [P1] Restore argv-based git invocation to prevent shell injection
findings.body: `execAsync` (promisified `exec`) runs its argument through a shell, so the `branch` parameter becomes shell syntax instead of a discrete argv element. Any `branch` value containing shell metacharacters — e.g. `main; touch /tmp/pwned`, `$(cmd)`, backticks, or `&&` — executes arbitrary OS commands with the process's privileges when `showBranch` is called. The previous code, `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])`, passed `branch` as a literal argument and was safe. Even non-malicious git-legal ref names containing shell-special characters (e.g. a ref with a single quote or parentheses) now fail to parse or behave unexpectedly. `showBranch` is exported, so every caller of this now-unsafe path is exposed; revert to the argv form (`execFileAsync`) or, if a shell is truly required, pass the command without interpolating `branch`.
